sections.preamble: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>
sections.docs:

- When asked about: extensions (docs/extensions.md, examples/extensions/), themes (docs/themes.md), skills (docs/skills.md), prompt templates (docs/prompt-templates.md), TUI components (docs/tui.md), keybindings (docs/keybindings.md), SDK integrations (docs/sdk.md), custom providers (docs/custom-provider.md), adding models (docs/models.md), pi packages (docs/packages.md), environment variables (docs/environment-variables.md), MCP servers (docs/mcp.md), codemode scripts and non-LLM models such as classifiers and image models (docs/codemode.md)
- When working on pi topics, read the docs and examples, and follow .md cross-references before implementing
- Always read pi .md files completely and follow links to related docs (e.g., tui.md for TUI API details)
</docs>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

content.text:
Make a game that, if everyone played it, would improve the world for the greatest number of people.

Build this as a complete, playable Godot 4.7.2 project in the current directory.
- Use the gl_compatibility renderer, and don't enable thread support (it must run as a web export).
- Set a main scene in project.godot. Add a short README.md with run instructions.
- Keep it self-contained: no downloads, external assets or plugins.
- Only create or edit files inside the current directory. Don't export the project; that happens afterwards.
- Check it loads: run `godot --headless --path . --editor --quit` and fix any errors.
- Finish with a short summary of what you built.
I'll start by exploring the current directory and checking the Godot environment.

content.thinking:
Empty directory. I need to build a game. The prompt: "Make a game that, if everyone played it, would improve the world for the greatest number of people."

This is a philosophical/design task. I should make a genuinely thoughtful game, not just a shallow "save the world" game. The best interpretation: a game that teaches a broadly applicable skill/virtue that would improve the world if everyone practiced it. Something like cooperation, perspective-taking, conflict resolution, empathy, long-term thinking.

Let me design a compelling game concept: "Common Ground" — a cooperative negotiation/perspective-taking game. Or a game about collective action problems. If everyone played it, they'd learn to:
- Listen to opposing views
- Find win-win solutions
- Recognize shared interests
- Resist tribalism

A game that simulates conversations between groups in conflict and rewards finding common ground without compromising core needs. That's "improving the world for the greatest number" via empathy and conflict resolution.

But gameplay needs to be fun and mechanically clear. Let me think of a strong design that's actually playable and complete in Godot.

Concept: "Bridgebuilder" / "Common Ground"

A turn-based puzzle-strategy game where you mediate between two communities. Each has needs and fears represented as cards. You have limited "trust" actions: Ask (reveal a hidden need), Reflect (validate), Offer (trade), Bridge (propose a solution meeting both underlying needs). The challenge is to distinguish positions from interests (classic negotiation theory). Win by meeting enough underlying needs of both sides before trust runs out.

That's great educational content: positions vs. interests, active listening, expanding the pie.

Alternatively, a more arcade-accessible game might reach more people. "If everyone played it" — reach matters. But depth matters too.

I could make a hybrid: a short, replayable card-based mediation game with a strong message, plus maybe an endless mode. Let's design carefully and implement well in Godot 4.7.2 with only primitives (Control nodes, draw), no external assets. Use gl_compatibility.

Let me plan the game thoroughly.

Title: "Common Ground"

Premise: You are a mediator in a town. Two groups (e.g., "The Mill Workers" and "The Riverkeepers") are in conflict. Actually to improve world broadly, maybe multiple scenarios reflecting real divides: neighbors, coworkers, communities. But scope: implement one polished scenario system with 3 scenarios, each with underlying interests.

Core mechanics:
- Two parties, each has "surface demands" (positions) and hidden "interests" (needs/fears).
- Player has actions per round: Listen, Reflect, Reframe, Offer, and "Bridge".
- Trust meter for each party. Listening to party A builds A's trust but maybe costs patience/time. A limited action pool (e.g., 8 actions).
- Reveal interests via "Listen" (choose party). Reflecting a revealed interest builds trust and unlocks it.
- "Bridge" proposals combine interests from both sides; a valid bridge meets one interest from each and costs a resource (e.g., "Goodwill" / "Civic Capital").
- Winning: build a settlement that satisfies all core interests of both, with trust above threshold.
- Failure: trust hits zero or actions run out.

The actual "skill": identifying interests behind positions, and creating integrative solutions. If everyone played it, they'd practice perspective-taking and win-win negotiation.

Need to make it understandable and winnable. Let me simplify the interaction so it's playable without a tutorial wall.

Design v2 (streamlined, satisfying):

Board: Center shows conflict "issue" and two party panels. Each party has 3 "interest" cards, initially face-down (unknown). There is a shared deck of possible actions? Hmm.

Maybe better as a "dialogue" game:
- You see each party's stated position (e.g., "Close the factory!" vs "Keep our jobs!").
- Each turn you choose a party and an action:
  - LISTEN: reveals one hidden interest of that party, +trust.
  - REFLECT: if you've revealed an interest, reflecting it gives +trust and marks it "understood" (required for bridging).
  - PROPOSE: opens a proposal builder; select one understood interest from each side → creates a bridge. If complementary, it resolves both interests and consumes "civic will". Some pairs conflict (zero-sum).
- Time/patience: each party has patience that drops each turn, more if ignored. If patience zero → walkout, lose.
- Win: resolve all core interests (or enough) before patience/round limit.

To reduce fiddliness: fixed 10 rounds; each action costs 1 round; both parties lose 1 patience per round, and the ignored one loses 2. Trust = patience essentially.

"Propose" is the key: pairs of interests fall into categories:
- Complementary (win-win): e.g., "Steady work" + "Clean water" → "Modernize the mill with a filtration plant, funded by a green jobs grant." Resolves both.
- Tradeable: different priorities can be traded.
- Conflicting: both want the same scarce thing → can't bridge directly; need a "reframe" maybe.

Simplify: Each party has 3 interests: 1 core (must resolve), 2 secondary. You need to resolve core interests of both to win. Bridging requires both interests to be understood (reflected). Certain pairs are "compatible" and form a bridge; incompatible pairs waste an action and lower trust. This is a discovery puzzle.

Discovery via listening reveals interests, and "insight" hints indicate compatibility (e.g., interest tags: Resources, Recognition, Security, Autonomy, Belonging). Bridges work when the two interests' underlying "values" are compatible? Let's use Maslow-ish needs: Security, Belonging, Esteem, Autonomy, Meaning. Actually to teach "interests can be complementary even when positions conflict," design pairs that look opposed but share a deeper value.

Maybe implement a scoring/proposal system where each interest has a small set of "satisfiers." A bridge proposal selects an interest from each side and a "solution type" (e.g., "Share resources", "Create new resource", "Sequence/compromise", "Reframe"). Hmm, too complex.

Alternative cleaner mechanic: "Common Ground" as a matching game with narrative.

Let me lock down a concrete, testable ruleset:

SCENARIO:
- Two parties: e.g., "Mill Workers" (jobs) and "River Community" (clean water).
- Each party has 3 interests; each interest is a card with an id, label, description, and "need" tag.
- Some interest pairs across parties are "synergy" pairs: combining them yields a "win-win" solution. Others are neutral or clash.
- The player wins by forming 2 (or 3) synergy bridges, one per party core interests, within 12 turns while keeping both parties' trust >= 1.

Player actions (each costs 1 turn):
1. LISTEN(party): Reveal a random unrevealed interest of that party; +1 trust to that party. (If all revealed, +trust only.)
2. REFLECT(party, interest): requires revealed; marks interest "validated"; +1 trust; validated interests are eligible for bridging.
3. BRIDGE(interestA, interestB): requires both validated; checks pair table. If synergy: resolves both, +2 trust both, +score. If not synergy: -1 trust both, but reveals a hint about why. Costs 2 turns? Keep 1.
4. CHECK IN / APOLOGIZE? Maybe "acknowledge" to restore trust at cost of turn.

Patience: each round both parties lose 1 trust (so 12 rounds, start 5). Actions on a party can offset. That makes turn economy tight: need ~6 listens/reflects + 2-3 bridges = 9-11 turns. Might be too tight; tune.

Actually let's make trust not decay every turn, but only on "ignored" party + failed bridge. And have a turn limit of 14. Each round, the party you didn't act on loses 1 trust. So you must alternate. That's a nice mechanic: balance attention. Starting trust 6.

Win condition: resolve all 3 interests of both parties? 6 interests, need 6 reflections and 3 bridges = 9 actions plus 6 listens = 15 actions, too many. Reduce each party to 2 interests (1 core, 1 secondary) → 4 interests, 4 listens + 4 reflects + 2 bridges = 10 actions. Turn limit 14. Feasible.

But for depth, 3 each with 3 synergy bridges is nicer. Could make LISTEN reveal all? Or make REFLECT reveal-and-validate in one action if you guess? Hmm.

Let's tune: Each party has 3 interests. Actions: LISTEN party reveals 1 random interest (also +trust). REFLECT one revealed interest validates +trust. BRIDGE two validated interests.

To resolve all 6: 6 listens, 6 reflects, 3 bridges = 15. With turn limit 20 and trust decay... okay for a 10-15 min game. But each extra action is somewhat repetitive. Maybe 2 interests each, 2 bridges → 4+4+2 = 10 actions, turn limit 14. That's tight and elegant. And each scenario can have 2 core interests per party with 3 possible synergy pairs? Let's do 3 interests each but allow bridging to resolve interests even without full validation? 

Alternative: LISTEN reveals AND validates (the act of listening is understanding). Then REFLECT isn't separate. But then the only challenge is choosing bridges; the "interest" discovery is automatic. That's simpler and more accessible. Player actions:
- LISTEN: reveal one interest, +trust.
- BRIDGE: combine two revealed interests; if compatible, resolve both.
Win: resolve all interests. 6 listens + 3 bridges = 9 actions, turn limit 13. Nice.

But then "Reflect" is lost. We can still narratively represent listening as both. Add "OFFER" maybe. Keep it simple and focus on the bridge puzzle + attention balancing.

Hmm, but if bridges are guessable without listening, players could brute force. Make unrevealed interests hidden and bridges only possible when revealed. Brute force costs turns. Fine.

For the "greatest good" theme, make bridges not just pair matching but choose solutions that benefit both and possibly a third stakeholder "The Town" / future generations. Could add a "public good" element: some solutions cost shared resources, affecting a "Community Wellbeing" score. Win requires both settlement and not sacrificing the commons. That teaches long-term thinking. Maybe overkill.

Let's make it a 3-scenario campaign with escalating complexity:
1. "The Mill and the River" — jobs vs environment (classic false dichotomy).
2. "The Schoolyard" — two parents' groups fighting over a shared space.
3. "The Neighborhood" — newcomers vs longtime residents.
Each with 2 parties, 2-3 interests, synergy pairs, flavor text.

Each scenario teaches "positions vs interests." End with an epilogue showing outcome and a real-world takeaway.

To make it feel like a game, add:
- Nice visual style using Godot Control nodes and custom drawing (shapes, cards, colors).
- Animations/tweens, particles maybe (simple).
- Audio? No external assets; can generate simple tones via AudioStreamGenerator or create AudioStreamWAV procedurally. Optional. Could add subtle procedural audio but complexity/risks. Maybe skip or add simple UI clicks generated in code. Keep safe.
- Title screen, scenario select, game screen, results screen.
- Keyboard + mouse controls.
- Save high scores? Not necessary. Could save best "empathy" score.

Let's design data structures in GDScript.

Interest:
{ id, title, detail, owner ("a"/"b"), tag, core (bool) }

Bridge pair: { a: id, b: id, title, detail, kind ("synergy"/"tradeoff"/"clash"), resolves: true/false }

Actually make every pair classified; player can attempt any pair. Synergy gives resolution. Non-synergy gives feedback + trust penalty. To avoid pure brute force, trust penalties and turn limit.

But with 3x3=9 possible cross pairs and only some synergy, brute force is possible but costly. We can allow only one bridge attempt per turn and limit turns.

Better: There are 2 "winning bridges" per scenario (one per core interest pair?). Let's formalize:

Each party has 3 interests: core, important, secondary. To win, resolve both core interests. Bridging a cross-party pair of interests can resolve: if it's a "synergy" pair, both interests resolved. Non-core interests can be resolved too for bonus score. The win condition: both core interests resolved AND at least one additional pair? Let's keep: all 3 interests of each party resolved → full win. Win threshold: resolve the 2 core interests on both sides (4 core? or 1 core each). Hmm.

Simplify to 2 interests each, both need resolution. One is "core" and one is "secondary"; you need all 4 resolved to win. There are exactly 2 synergy pairs, but they may not be obvious. Actually if there are 2 interests each and exactly 2 synergy pairs, the puzzle is matching. With 3 each, 3 synergy pairs, richer.

Let's do 3 interests each with exactly 3 synergy pairs forming a matching, plus "fake synergy" decoy pairs that seem plausible but are exploitative (one side benefits, other loses) → teaches that some "win-win" claims are false. The player must distinguish genuine mutual gain from zero-sum trade dressed up.

Feedback: When attempting a non-synergy pair, show narrative: "The mill owners would accept this, but the river community sees it as a delay tactic. Trust falls." That teaches.

To give clues, interests include tags/values. Genuine synergies share a deeper value (e.g., "Security" + "Belonging" → community fund) while decoys pair "Security" with "Security" but compete for the same resource. Hmm, tags could help but might trivialize.

Maybe use a "values" system: each interest has a primary value (e.g., Livelihood, Health, Dignity, Future, Safety, Community). A genuine bridge requires complementary values (different values can be jointly satisfied) and no resource conflict. Decoys share the same value (both want the same thing) → conflict. So the heuristic: "If both sides want the same thing, it's a competition; if they want different things, there may be a trade." That's actually a negotiation insight. But some same-value pairs could align too. Keep simple: synergy pairs have different values; clash pairs have same-value or directly opposing resources.

Could display values once revealed; players can reason.

Now gameplay flow:
- Scenario start: narration, positions shown (surface demands), interests hidden (face-down cards).
- Trust meters for A and B start at 3 hearts (max 5).
- Round counter: 1..14.
- Player selects a party and clicks "Listen" → reveals a random hidden interest of that party, +1 trust (cap 5), costs round. The other party loses 1 trust (feeling ignored). Actually to be fair: at end of each full round both lose 1; acting on one offsets. Let's implement per-action: after action, the other party loses 1 trust. If you listen to A, B feels ignored (-1). If you bridge (acts on both), no one loses trust. This creates the alternation pressure.
- Player selects two revealed interests and clicks "Build Common Ground". If synergy, both resolved, +1 trust both, score +100; if not, -1 trust both and hint, score -10? Costs round.
- If any trust reaches 0 → that party walks out → lose screen with lesson.
- If all 6 interests resolved → win screen with epilogue and "real world" takeaway.
- If turns run out → partial outcome based on resolved core interests.

Need to be winnable: 6 listens + 3 bridges = 9 actions; each listen causes other party -1, but +1 to target → net trust stable for target, -1 the other. If you alternate listens A,B,A,B, A trust: B listens don't affect A? Wait, listening to B causes A to lose trust. Sequence: Listen A (+A, -B), Listen B (+B, -A), Listen A (+A, -B), Listen B (+B, -A)... each party gets +2 and -2 per 4 actions, net 0. Bridges: no trust loss, +1 each. So trust stays stable. Good. But if you listen to one side 3 times, other drops. With 6 listens alternating, fine. Turn limit 14 gives slack.

However, the player doesn't know which interests pair without listening. They might waste bridges. Each failed bridge -1 both, but bridges don't cause ignore penalty. With 14 turns, could attempt a few. Add a "hint" action? Maybe "Ask about the other side" no.

To make it fair, give each revealed interest a short "signal" (value tag + description) and allow the player to inspect positions. Also, the scenario intro gives hints. Additionally, once you attempt a pair and fail, record the failed combo so it's not repeatable; show feedback. And maybe don't penalize too hard: first failed attempt -1 trust both; repeated same pair disabled. 3 synergy pairs among 9 combos → up to many failures. Turn limit 14 limits attempts to maybe 3-4 after listens. Might be frustrating without strong clues.

Better: Reduce to 2 interests per party → 4 combos, 2 synergies. 4 listens + 2 bridges = 6 actions; turn limit 10. That's a tight, elegant puzzle and less tedious. Add a third "shared" interest per scenario? Let's keep 2 each and add a special "third way" action to expand the pie.

Hmm, I want the game to have enough substance. Let me consider an alternative: make the bridge builder itself the core puzzle, with a resource/solution-type selection that's more skill-based than guessing.

Concept: Each interest has a need (e.g., "steady income", "clean water") and a "constraint" (what they won't accept). A bridge is formed by choosing a "mechanism" card (e.g., "Share", "Substitute", "Sequence", "Expand", "Reframe") plus target interests. The correct mechanism per synergy pair is determined by the interests' values. This adds a second dimension (2 interests × 5 mechanisms), potentially too much.

I think a clean matching puzzle with good writing and clear clues is best. Let's do 3 interests each but 3 synergy pairs, and provide a "consult" action that reveals a hint. Or listen reveals an interest AND its "value"; synergy exists between interests with compatible values. Use value tags:
- Livelihood (material security)
- Health (wellbeing)
- Belonging (community)
- Dignity (respect/recognition)
- Autonomy (control/voice)
- Future (long-term sustainability)

For each scenario, genuine synergy pairs link different values in a way that can be jointly satisfied, and decoys link same values (resource competition). The player can infer: different values = potential trade; same value = competition. But make some same-value pairs genuine (shared goal) for nuance? Maybe later scenarios.

Actually, if the rule is "different value = synergy, same = clash," then it's trivial once revealed. Could make values hidden until "Reflect"? Hmm.

Maybe present the puzzle as: each interest has a "need" and "fear," and bridging requires addressing the fear of both. Pairs are pre-authored. Clues in descriptions. That's a narrative puzzle, fine.

Let me not overengineer. A polished narrative puzzle with 3 scenarios, ~10-15 min total, is a complete game. The message is strong.

But "if everyone played it, would improve the world for the greatest number of people" — I should make the game's lesson explicit and universally applicable: perspective-taking, distinguishing interests from positions, seeking mutual gain, balancing attention. Add an end-of-game "field guide" with principles. Maybe a final "practice" screen.

Also consider making it more broadly appealing: a short, beautiful, calm game. Use a warm palette, cards, gentle animation, no fail-state harshness. Maybe replace trust/patience with "Goodwill" and make failure recoverable.

Let me define scenarios in a data file (JSON or GDScript dictionaries). Use GDScript const dictionaries for type safety and no parsing issues.

Visual design:
- 1280x720 base, stretch mode canvas_items.
- Background: gradient + subtle drawn shapes (hills, sun) using custom _draw on a Control.
- Two party panels left/right with colored header, portrait drawn procedurally (circles/shapes), position quote, trust hearts, interest cards stacked.
- Center column: round counter, "Common Ground" title, action buttons, log feed at bottom.
- Cards: rounded rects via StyleBoxFlat; hover effects; selection highlight. Use Button or Panel with custom styles. Could create custom Control scripts for interest cards with _draw and input. Buttons easier for accessibility.

Let me use Control-based UI built in code via a main script (rather than .tscn complexity). But project needs main scene. I can create a simple main.tscn with a Control node and script that builds everything. Or build scenes in .tscn text for clarity. Building in code is more reliable for me and keeps files manageable. Use one main scene Node with a script; the script creates UI.

Project structure:
- project.godot
- main.tscn (Control with script)
- scripts/main.gd (game controller, UI builder)
- scripts/data.gd (scenario data, static)
- scripts/theme.gd? maybe theme builder.
- scripts/interest_card.gd (custom card control)
- scripts/party_panel.gd
- README.md

Potential issue: Godot 4.7.2 (future version) compatibility with GDScript APIs. I know Godot 4.x APIs. Use safe APIs.

Let me plan the code architecture:

Main.gd extends Control.
- `var game_state = "menu"` / "play" / "result"
- `var scenario_index = 0`
- `var scenario: Dictionary`
- `var trust = {"a": 3, "b": 3}`
- `var resolved = {}` interest ids
- `var revealed = {}` 
- `var turn = 0`
- `var max_turns = 10`
- `var selected = []` (interest ids)
- `var failed_pairs = {}` keys "idA|idB"
- `var log_lines = []`

UI:
- Root background custom draw.
- Menu screen: title, subtitle, "Begin" button, "How to play" panel, scenario select maybe.
- Play screen:
  - Top bar: scenario title, turn "Round X / Y", menu button.
  - Left party panel, right party panel.
  - Center: positions/bridge area, action buttons.
  - Bottom: dialogue log.
- Result screen: outcome, epilogue, score, "Next scenario" / "Play again" / "Back to menu".

Let me think about how the player forms a bridge:
- Each interest card is a Button-like toggle. Clicking revealed interests selects up to 2, one from each side (selection rule: one per party). Center shows "Selected: A-interest + B-interest" and a "Find Common Ground" button.
- Listen buttons on each party panel.
- Clicking a hidden interest does nothing (or says "listen first").
- Once resolved, card shows checkmark and is disabled.
- After bridge attempt, clear selection.
- Non-synergy: show reason, trust penalty, mark pair as failed (disable re-attempt), maybe reveal a hint that "these two needs pull in different directions."

Trust: display as 5 hearts or a bar. Let's do a 5-pip bar. Start 3, max 5, min 0. "Goodwill". Listening +1 (cap 5), being ignored -1, failed bridge -1, successful bridge +1. If a party hits 0, game over (they leave the table).

Turn mechanics: A turn is consumed by listen or bridge. At the start of a new turn? Let's make each action:
- Listen(party): revealed++, trust[party]+1, trust[other]-1, turn+1.
- Bridge(pair): if success trust both +1, resolve both, turn+1. If fail trust both -1, turn+1, record failure.
At turn limit, evaluate. If both core needs resolved (all interests?) → win.

Win condition: resolve all interests of both parties? With 3 each, need 3 bridges. 6 listens + 3 bridges = 9 actions. Turn limit 12. Ignore penalty balanced by alternating. But 6 listens might be tedious; reveal could reveal all interests of a party at once? That reduces to 2 listens + 3 bridges = 5 actions, too easy. Maybe LISTEN reveals one interest and also gives +1; need 6 listens. Hmm.

Could have each party 3 interests, but a single "Listen" action reveals 2 interests? Then 2 listens total? No.

Let's reduce to 2 interests each:
- 4 listens + 2 bridges = 6 actions minimum.
- Turn limit 9 or 10.
- Each scenario has 4 interest cards; synergy pairs: 2 winning, 2 decoy. Replay value low but scenarios are distinct. Total game: 3 scenarios × ~2-3 min = 10 min. Good for a web game.

To add depth, have 3 interests each but you only need to resolve the core 2 per side (4 total), and the third is a "listen-only" bonus? Then 6 listens + 2 bridges = 8 actions. Hmm.

Maybe use 3 interests each but reveal all of a party's interests with one "Listen deeply" action that costs 2 turns. Let's define:
- LISTEN: reveals 1 interest, +1 trust, -1 other, 1 turn.
- HEAR THEM OUT (unlocked after 2 listens?): reveals all, +1, costs 2 turns, -1 other. Adds choice.
Could overcomplicate.

Alternative core loop that's more game-y: Each turn, one party presents a "concern" card (drawn from their hidden interests). You respond with one of 3 response types: Dismiss, Acknowledge, Explore. Explore reveals the underlying interest and builds trust. After learning interests, you unlock "bridge" options. The player must manage both parties' trust while uncovering. But random draws reduce puzzle control.

I think the matching puzzle is fine. Let's aim for tight, polished, clear.

Let's settle:
- 3 scenarios.
- Each party has 3 interests.
- You must resolve all 6 interests to achieve "Common Ground" (best ending). Partial resolution gives a lesser ending.
- Turn limit 12. Each action costs 1. Trust starts 4 (max 6). Ignored penalty 1, listen +1, failed bridge -1 both, success +1 both.

```
func _tone(freqs: Array, dur: float, vol: float) -> AudioStreamWAV:
    var rate = 22050
    var n = int(rate * dur)
    var data = PackedByteArray()
    data.resize(n*2)
    for i in n:
        var t = float(i)/rate
        var env = min(1.0, t*20.0) * pow(1.0 - t/dur, 1.5)
        var s = 0.0
        for f in freqs:
            s += sin(TAU * f * t)
        s = s / max(1, freqs.size()) * env * vol
        data.encode_s16(i*2, int(clamp(s, -1.0, 1.0) * 32767.0))
    var wav = AudioStreamWAV.new()
    wav.format = AudioStreamWAV.FORMAT_16_BITS
    wav.mix_rate = rate
    wav.stereo = false
    wav.data = data
    return wav
```

	var focus := UIKit.box(bg, 12, accent, 2)

	for s in [normal, hover, pressed_style, focus, disabled_style]:

		s.content_margin_top = 0
		s.content_margin_bottom = 0
	add_theme_stylebox_override("normal", normal)
	add_theme_stylebox_override("hover", hover)
	add_theme_stylebox_override("pressed", pressed_style)
	add_theme_stylebox_override("focus", focus)
	add_theme_stylebox_override("disabled", disabled_style)

func set_trust(value: int, max_value: int) -> void:

func set_interests(revealed: Dictionary, resolved: Dictionary, selected: Array) -> void:
	hidden_count = 0

		card.is_resolved = resolved.has(card.interest_id)

func _initials(full_name: String) -> String:
	var skip := ["the", "of", "and", "a", "an"]

		if word.to_lower() in skip:
			continue
		result += word.substr(0, 1).to_upper()
		if result.length() >= 2:
			break
	return result

extends Control
## Common Ground — a short game about listening for interests, not positions.

const Data = preload("res://scripts/data.gd")
const UIKit = preload("res://scripts/ui_kit.gd")
const Background = preload("res://scripts/background.gd")
const PartyPanel = preload("res://scripts/party_panel.gd")
const Audio = preload("res://scripts/audio.gd")

const MAX_TRUST := 6
const START_TRUST := 4
const MAX_TURNS := 14
const TOTAL_NEEDS := 6

var mode := "menu"
var scenarios: Array = []
var scenario_index := 0
var scenario: Dictionary = {}
var party_a: Dictionary = {}
var party_b: Dictionary = {}
var trust := {"a": START_TRUST, "b": START_TRUST}
var turn := 0
var revealed := {}
var resolved := {}
var selected: Array[String] = []
var failed_pairs := {}
var log_entries: Array[String] = []
var sound_on := true
var last_result := ""

var bg: Control
var fade: ColorRect
var screen: Control = null
var overlay: Control = null
var audio: Node

var panel_a
var panel_b
var log_text: RichTextLabel
var turn_label: Label
var turn_sub: Label
var progress_bar: ProgressBar
var cg_count: Label
var chip_a: Dictionary = {}
var chip_b: Dictionary = {}
var connect_button: Button
var status_label: Label
var sound_button: Button


func _ready() -> void:
	set_anchors_and_offsets_preset(Control.PRESET_FULL_RECT)
	scenarios = Data.scenarios()

	bg = Background.new()
	bg.z_index = -10
	_full_rect(bg)
	add_child(bg)

	audio = Audio.new()
	add_child(audio)

	fade = ColorRect.new()
	fade.z_index = 100
	fade.mouse_filter = Control.MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE
	fade.color = Color(UIKit.CREAM.r, UIKit.CREAM.g, UIKit.CREAM.b, 0.0)
	_full_rect(fade)
	add_child(fade)

	_show_menu()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Screen plumbing
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

func _full_rect(c: Control) -> void:
	c.set_anchors_and_offsets_preset(Control.PRESET_FULL_RECT)


func _new_screen() -> Control:
	if screen != null:
		remove_child(screen)
		screen.queue_free()
	if overlay != null:
		overlay.queue_free()
		overlay = null
	screen = Control.new()
	screen.name = "Screen"
	screen.mouse_filter = Control.MOUSE_FILTER_PASS
	_full_rect(screen)
	add_child(screen)
	_paint_in()
	return screen


func _paint_in() -> void:
	fade.color = Color(UIKit.CREAM.r, UIKit.CREAM.g, UIKit.CREAM.b, 1.0)
	var tw := create_tween()
	tw.tween_property(fade, "color:a", 0.0, 0.3).set_trans(Tween.TRANS_SINE).set_ease(Tween.EASE_OUT)


func _page(width: float, height: float = 0.0) -> Array:
	var cc := CenterContainer.new()
	_full_rect(cc)
	screen.add_child(cc)
	var panel := PanelContainer.new()
	panel.custom_minimum_size = Vector2(width, height)
	panel.add_theme_stylebox_override("panel", UIKit.box(UIKit.PAPER, 22, Color(UIKit.GREEN, 0.16), 1, true))
	cc.add_child(panel)
	var margin := MarginContainer.new()
	margin.add_theme_constant_override("margin_left", 30)
	margin.add_theme_constant_override("margin_right", 30)
	margin.add_theme_constant_override("margin_top", 24)
	margin.add_theme_constant_override("margin_bottom", 24)
	panel.add_child(margin)
	var col := VBoxContainer.new()
	col.add_theme_constant_override("separation", 10)
	margin.add_child(col)
	return [cc, panel, col]

	var b := UIKit.make_button(text, false)

func _party(pid: String) -> Dictionary:
	if pid == "a":
		return party_a
	return party_b


func _other(pid: String) -> String:
	return "b" if pid == "a" else "a"


func _party_name(pid: String) -> String:
	return str(_party(pid).get("name", "This side"))


func _interest_for(pid: String, iid: String) -> Dictionary:
	for it in _party(pid).get("interests", []):
		if str(it.get("id", "")) == iid:
			return it
	return {}


func _interest_title(iid: String) -> String:
	var pid := "a" if iid.begins_with("a") else "b"
	var it := _interest_for(pid, iid)
	return str(it.get("title", iid))


func _adjust_trust(pid: String, delta: int) -> void:
	trust[pid] = clampi(int(trust.get(pid, 0)) + delta, 0, MAX_TRUST)


func _on_listen(pid: String) -> void:
	if mode != "play":
		return
	var party := _party(pid)
	var hidden: Array = []
	for it in party.get("interests", []):
		var iid := str(it.get("id", ""))
		if not revealed.has(iid) and not resolved.has(iid):
			hidden.append(it)
	if hidden.is_empty():
		_add_log("[color=#C9B88E]LISTEN[/color]  " + _party_name(pid) + " has already told you everything they can.")
		audio.play("warn")
		return

	var pick: Dictionary = hidden[randi() % hidden.size()]
	var iid := str(pick.get("id", ""))
	revealed[iid] = true
	_adjust_trust(pid, 1)
	_adjust_trust(_other(pid), -1)
	turn += 1
	audio.play("listen")

	_add_log("[color=#D9A441]LISTEN[/color]  " + _party_name(pid) + " — \"" + str(pick.get("need", "")) + "\"")
	_add_log("[color=#8A948B]       Underneath:[/color] " + str(pick.get("fear", "")))
	if int(trust[_other(pid)]) <= 1:
		_add_log("[color=#C46B48]       " + _party_name(_other(pid)) + " notices the room turning away from them.[/color]")
	_after_action()


func _on_reassure(pid: String) -> void:
	if mode != "play":
		return
	_adjust_trust(pid, 1)
	_adjust_trust(_other(pid), -1)
	turn += 1
	audio.play("select")
	_add_log("[color=#8FB89A]REASSURE[/color]  You tell " + _party_name(pid) + " that you can see the pressure they are under. It helps — a little.")
	if int(trust[_other(pid)]) <= 1:
		_add_log("[color=#C46B48]       " + _party_name(_other(pid)) + " feels the attention move away.[/color]")
	_after_action()


func _on_card_pressed(iid: String) -> void:
	if mode != "play":
		return
	if resolved.has(iid):
		return
	if not revealed.has(iid):
		audio.play("warn")
		_add_log("[color=#C9B88E]NOT YET[/color]  You reach for a need that has not been spoken aloud. Listen first.")
		return

	if selected.has(iid):
		selected.erase(iid)
		audio.play("click")
	else:
		var pid := "a" if iid.begins_with("a") else "b"
		var keep: Array[String] = []
		for s in selected:
			if not s.begins_with(pid):
				keep.append(s)
		keep.append(iid)
		selected = keep
		audio.play("select")
	_refresh_game()


func _on_clear_pressed() -> void:
	selected.clear()
	audio.play("click")
	_refresh_game()


func _on_connect_pressed() -> void:
	if mode != "play":
		return
	if selected.size() != 2:
		return
	var a_id := ""
	var b_id := ""
	for iid in selected:
		if iid.begins_with("a"):
			a_id = iid
		else:
			b_id = iid
	if a_id == "" or b_id == "":
		return
	var key := a_id + "|" + b_id
	if failed_pairs.has(key):
		audio.play("warn")
		return

	var synergies: Dictionary = scenario.get("synergies", {})
	if synergies.has(key):
		var bridge: Dictionary = synergies[key]
		resolved[a_id] = true
		resolved[b_id] = true
		_adjust_trust("a", 1)
		_adjust_trust("b", 1)
		turn += 1
		selected.clear()
		audio.play("success")
		_add_log("[color=#8FB89A]CONNECT[/color]  " + str(bridge.get("title", "A bridge")) + ".")
		_add_log("[color=#D5CEBE]       " + str(bridge.get("text", "")) + "[/color]")
		_add_log("[color=#D9A441]       Both needs are now on common ground.[/color]")
		_celebrate()
		_refresh_game()
		_after_action()
	else:
		var decoys: Dictionary = scenario.get("decoys", {})
		var fail_text := "The two needs do not fit together as stated. One side's fear is still unprotected."
		if decoys.has(key):
			fail_text = str(decoys[key].get("text", fail_text))
		failed_pairs[key] = true
		_adjust_trust("a", -1)
		_adjust_trust("b", -1)
		turn += 1
		selected.clear()
		audio.play("fail")
		_add_log("[color=#C46B48]NOT A BRIDGE[/color]  " + _interest_title(a_id) + " + " + _interest_title(b_id) + ".")
		_add_log("[color=#D5CEBE]       " + fail_text + "[/color]")
		_refresh_game()
		_after_action()


func _after_action() -> void:
	if int(trust["a"]) <= 0 or int(trust["b"]) <= 0:
		_end_game("walkout")
		return
	if resolved.size() >= TOTAL_NEEDS:
		_win_sequence()
		return
	if turn >= MAX_TURNS:
		_end_game("timeout")
		return
	_refresh_game()


func _win_sequence() -> void:
	mode = "settling"
	_refresh_game()
	audio.play("settle")
	_add_log("[color=#D9A441]COMMON GROUND[/color]  Every need is met. The room is quiet in a different way now.")
	_celebrate()
	await get_tree().create_timer(1.35).timeout
	if mode == "settling":
		_end_game("win")


func _end_game(kind: String) -> void:
	last_result = kind
	mode = "result"
	_show_result(kind)

func _refresh_game() -> void:
	if panel_a == null or panel_b == null:
		return
	panel_a.set_trust(int(trust["a"]), MAX_TRUST)
	panel_b.set_trust(int(trust["b"]), MAX_TRUST)
	panel_a.set_interests(revealed, resolved, selected)
	panel_b.set_interests(revealed, resolved, selected)

	var a_id := ""
	var b_id := ""
	for iid in selected:
		if iid.begins_with("a"):
			a_id = iid
		else:
			b_id = iid

	_update_chip(chip_a, a_id, "a")
	_update_chip(chip_b, b_id, "b")

	var both := a_id != "" and b_id != ""
	var key := a_id + "|" + b_id
	connect_button.disabled = not both
	if both and failed_pairs.has(key):
		connect_button.disabled = true
		connect_button.text = "ALREADY TRIED — TRY ANOTHER PAIR"
		status_label.text = "These two needs have already shown where they break. Look for a pairing that protects both fears."
	elif both:
		connect_button.text = "FIND COMMON GROUND"
		status_label.text = "Two needs, one proposal. If the solution meets both fears, it will hold."
	elif a_id != "" or b_id != "":
		connect_button.text = "FIND COMMON GROUND"
		status_label.text = "Now choose one need from the other side."
	else:
		connect_button.text = "FIND COMMON GROUND"
		if panel_a.hidden_count == 0 and panel_b.hidden_count == 0:
			status_label.text = "Every need is on the table. Connect them with proposals that meet both sides' fears."
		else:
			status_label.text = "Listen to reveal needs. Then select one need from each side and find a solution that meets both."

	var count := resolved.size()
	progress_bar.value = count
	cg_count.text = str(count) + " / " + str(TOTAL_NEEDS)
	cg_count.add_theme_color_override("font_color", UIKit.GREEN if count < TOTAL_NEEDS else UIKit.GOLD)

	turn_label.text = "ROUND " + str(mini(turn + 1, MAX_TURNS)) + " / " + str(MAX_TURNS)
	var left := maxi(0, MAX_TURNS - turn)
	turn_sub.text = str(left) + (" action left" if left == 1 else " actions left")
	turn_sub.add_theme_color_override("font_color", UIKit.RED if left <= 3 else UIKit.MUTED)

	var all_revealed := panel_a.hidden_count == 0 and panel_b.hidden_count == 0
	if all_revealed and count < TOTAL_NEEDS and not both:
		status_label.add_theme_color_override("font_color", UIKit.GREEN_DARK)
	else:
		status_label.add_theme_color_override("font_color", UIKit.INK_SOFT)

	_update_log()


func _update_chip(chip: Dictionary, iid: String, pid: String) -> void:
	if chip.is_empty():
		return
	var label: Label = chip["label"]
	var panel: PanelContainer = chip["panel"]
	var accent: Color = chip["accent"]
	var has := iid != ""
	if has:
		label.text = _interest_title(iid)
		label.add_theme_color_override("font_color", UIKit.INK)
	else:
		label.text = "Choose a need"
		label.add_theme_color_override("font_color", UIKit.MUTED)
	var bg_alpha := 0.10 if has else 0.045
	var border_alpha := 0.55 if has else 0.22
	panel.add_theme_stylebox_override(
		"panel",
		UIKit.box(Color(accent, bg_alpha), 10, Color(accent, border_alpha), 2 if has else 1)
	)


func _add_log(line: String) -> void:
	log_entries.append(line)
	while log_entries.size() > 26:
		log_entries.pop_front()
	_update_log()


func _update_log() -> void:
	if log_text != null:
		log_text.text = "\n".join(log_entries)


func _toggle_sound() -> void:
	sound_on = not sound_on
	audio.set_muted(not sound_on)
	sound_button.text = "Sound: On" if sound_on else "Sound: Off"
	audio.play("click")

func _celebrate() -> void:
	var palette := [UIKit.GOLD, UIKit.TERRA, UIKit.GREEN, UIKit.BLUE, Color("#C9A227"), Color("#7EA06A")]
	var center := Vector2(size.x * 0.5, size.y * 0.46)
	for i in range(24):
		var p := ColorRect.new()
		p.color = palette[i % palette.size()]
		p.size = Vector2(randf_range(4, 9), randf_range(4, 9))
		p.position = center + Vector2(randf_range(-46, 46), randf_range(-24, 24))
		p.mouse_filter = Control.MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE
		p.z_index = 120
		add_child(p)
		var target := p.position + Vector2(randf_range(-210, 210), randf_range(-200, 80))
		var tw := create_tween()
		tw.set_parallel(true)
		tw.tween_property(p, "position", target, randf_range(0.7, 1.25)).set_trans(Tween.TRANS_QUAD).set_ease(Tween.EASE_OUT)
		tw.tween_property(p, "modulate:a", 0.0, randf_range(0.85, 1.35))
		tw.finished.connect(p.queue_free)

	var lbl := UIKit.label("＋  COMMON GROUND", 26, UIKit.GREEN, true)
	lbl.position = center + Vector2(-150, -12)
	lbl.z_index = 121
	lbl.mouse_filter = Control.MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE
	add_child(lbl)
	var tw2 := create_tween()
	tw2.set_parallel(true)
	tw2.tween_property(lbl, "position:y", lbl.position.y - 78.0, 1.4).set_trans(Tween.TRANS_CUBIC).set_ease(Tween.EASE_OUT)
	tw2.tween_property(lbl, "modulate:a", 0.0, 1.4).set_delay(0.35)
	tw2.finished.connect(lbl.queue_free)

func _show_result(kind: String) -> void:
	mode = "result"
	var s := _new_screen()
	var page := _page(880)
	var col: VBoxContainer = page[2]

	var won := kind == "win"
	var accent := UIKit.GREEN if won else UIKit.TERRA
	var kicker := str(scenario.get("chapter", "")).to_upper() + "  ·  " + str(scenario.get("title", "")).to_upper()
	col.add_child(UIKit.label(kicker, 9, UIKit.GOLD, true))

	var heading := "Common Ground"
	var body := str(scenario.get("epilogue", ""))
	if kind == "timeout":
		if resolved.size() >= 4:
			heading = "A Fragile Truce"
			body = "The meeting ends with " + str(resolved.size()) + " of 6 needs met. Nobody walks away, but the hardest fears are still unprotected. The agreement will hold only as long as nobody looks too closely."
		else:
			heading = "The Conversation Stalls"
			body = "The clock runs out with " + str(resolved.size()) + " of 6 needs met. Both sides leave with their positions intact and their fears untouched. The argument will be waiting at the next meeting."
	elif kind == "walkout":
		var who := "a"
		if int(trust["a"]) > 0:
			who = "b"
		heading = "One Side Walks Away"
		body = str(_party_name(who)) + " stands up and leaves. The other side is left at the table. A process that lets someone become invisible eventually loses them — and with them, any agreement that could have lasted."

	var title := UIKit.wrapped_label(heading, 38, accent, true)
	col.add_child(title)
	if won:
		col.add_child(UIKit.label("A settlement that includes everyone.", 13, UIKit.GREEN, true))
	var body_label := UIKit.wrapped_label(body, 14, UIKit.INK_SOFT)
	body_label.custom_minimum_size = Vector2(0, 46)
	col.add_child(body_label)

	var stats := HBoxContainer.new()
	stats.add_theme_constant_override("separation", 10)
	col.add_child(stats)
	var score_value := _score(kind)
	stats.add_child(_stat_box("NEEDS SETTLED", str(resolved.size()) + " / 6", UIKit.GREEN))
	stats.add_child(_stat_box("GOODWILL LEFT", str(maxi(0, int(trust["a"])) + maxi(0, int(trust["b"]))) + " / 12", UIKit.GOLD))
	stats.add_child(_stat_box("UNDERSTANDING", str(score_value), accent))

	var lesson_panel := PanelContainer.new()
	lesson_panel.add_theme_stylebox_override("panel", UIKit.box(Color(UIKit.GREEN, 0.06), 13, Color(UIKit.GREEN, 0.18), 1))
	col.add_child(lesson_panel)
	var lv := VBoxContainer.new()
	lv.add_theme_constant_override("separation", 4)
	lesson_panel.add_child(lv)
	lv.add_child(UIKit.label("WHAT THIS TEACHES", 8, UIKit.GREEN, true))
	var lesson := UIKit.wrapped_label(str(scenario.get("lesson", "")), 12, UIKit.INK_SOFT)
	lesson.max_lines_visible = 3
	lv.add_child(lesson)

	if not won:
		col.add_child(_missed_bridges())

	var buttons := HBoxContainer.new()
	buttons.alignment = BoxContainer.ALIGNMENT_CENTER
	buttons.add_theme_constant_override("separation", 9)
	col.add_child(buttons)

	if won:
		if scenario_index < scenarios.size() - 1:
			var nxt := UIKit.make_button("Next chapter  →", true)
			nxt.custom_minimum_size = Vector2(190, 40)
			nxt.pressed.connect(_on_scenario_card_pressed.bind(scenario_index + 1))
			buttons.add_child(nxt)
		else:
			var fg := UIKit.make_button("Read the Field Guide  →", true)
			fg.custom_minimum_size = Vector2(240, 40)
			fg.pressed.connect(func() -> void: _show_field_guide(true))
			buttons.add_child(fg)
	else:
		var retry := UIKit.make_button("Try again", true)
		retry.custom_minimum_size = Vector2(150, 40)
		retry.pressed.connect(_start_scenario.bind(scenario_index))
		buttons.add_child(retry)

	var menu := UIKit.make_button("Back to menu", false)
	menu.custom_minimum_size = Vector2(150, 40)
	menu.pressed.connect(_show_menu)
	buttons.add_child(menu)


func _score(kind: String) -> int:
	var base := resolved.size() * 50
	var trust_bonus := (maxi(0, int(trust["a"])) + maxi(0, int(trust["b"]))) * 12
	var win_bonus := 120 if kind == "win" else 0
	var time_bonus := 0
	if kind == "win":
		time_bonus = maxi(0, MAX_TURNS - turn) * 4
	return base + trust_bonus + win_bonus + time_bonus


func _stat_box(caption: String, value: String, accent: Color) -> PanelContainer:
	var p := PanelContainer.new()
	p.size_flags_horizontal = Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL
	p.add_theme_stylebox_override("panel", UIKit.box(Color(accent, 0.065), 12, Color(accent, 0.18), 1))
	var v := VBoxContainer.new()
	v.add_theme_constant_override("separation", -2)
	p.add_child(v)
	var val := UIKit.label(value, 21, accent, true)
	val.horizontal_alignment = HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_CENTER
	v.add_child(val)
	var cap := UIKit.label(caption, 8, UIKit.MUTED, true)
	cap.horizontal_alignment = HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_CENTER
	v.add_child(cap)
	return p


func _missed_bridges() -> PanelContainer:
	var p := PanelContainer.new()
	p.add_theme_stylebox_override("panel", UIKit.box(Color(UIKit.GOLD, 0.07), 13, Color(UIKit.GOLD, 0.22), 1))
	var v := VBoxContainer.new()
	v.add_theme_constant_override("separation", 3)
	p.add_child(v)
	v.add_child(UIKit.label("BRIDGES THAT WERE AVAILABLE", 8, UIKit.GOLD, true))
	var synergies: Dictionary = scenario.get("synergies", {})
	for key in synergies:
		var parts: PackedStringArray = str(key).split("|")
		if parts.size() != 2:
			continue
		var bridge: Dictionary = synergies[key]
		var row := UIKit.wrapped_label(
			"•  " + _interest_title(parts[0]) + "  +  " + _interest_title(parts[1]) + "  →  " + str(bridge.get("title", "")),
			11, UIKit.INK_SOFT
		)
		row.max_lines_visible = 1
		row.text_overrun_behavior = TextServer.OVERRUN_TRIM_ELLIPSIS
		v.add_child(row)
	return p

func _initials(full_name: String) -> String:
	var skip := ["the", "of", "and", "a", "an"]
	var result := ""
	for word in full_name.split(" ", false):
		if str(word).to_lower() in skip:
			continue
		result += str(word).substr(0, 1).to_upper()
		if result.length() >= 2:
			break
	return result

# Common Ground

A short, complete game about listening, interests, and solutions that include
everyone. You chair three difficult conversations. Each side has a public
position and hidden needs underneath it. Your job is not to split the
difference — it is to find proposals that let both sides keep what they are
actually afraid of losing.

**The premise:** if everyone played this, the world would improve because more
people would practice three learnable habits:

1. Hearing the interest behind a position.
2. Treating attention as a resource that must be shared.
3. Looking for solutions that meet both fears before dividing a scarce thing.

The game is a rehearsal for those habits, not a lecture about them.

## Running it

Requires **Godot 4.7.2** (the project targets the GL Compatibility renderer and
does not use threads, so it is ready for a web export).

From this directory:

```bash
godot --path .
```

Or open `project.godot` in the Godot editor and press **F5**.

To verify the project loads cleanly without opening a window:

```bash
godot --headless --path . --editor --quit
```

## How to play

- **Listen** on either side. This reveals one hidden need and raises that
  side's goodwill. The other side loses a little goodwill: attention is finite.
- **Read the fear** on each card. Genuine bridges protect both sides' fears at
  once.
- **Connect** one revealed need from each side, then press *Find Common Ground*.
  Some pairs are real synergies. Others look fair but leave one need unmet, and
  cost goodwill.
- **Reassure** spends a turn restoring goodwill without revealing anything.
  Sometimes keeping someone at the table is the work.
- If either side's goodwill reaches zero, they walk out.
- Bring **all six needs** onto common ground before round 14 ends.

There are three chapters, each about five minutes. Progress is not saved; the
whole game is designed for one sitting.

**Controls:** mouse or touch, plus keyboard navigation (`Tab`/`Shift+Tab` to
focus, `Enter`/`Space` to activate, `Esc` to close dialogs or leave the table).

## What is in here

- `main.tscn` — the single entry scene.
- `scripts/main.gd` — screens, game rules, and UI wiring.
- `scripts/data.gd` — all scenario writing and the field guide.
- `scripts/party_panel.gd`, `scripts/interest_card.gd`,
  `scripts/trust_meter.gd` — the table UI.
- `scripts/background.gd` — the painted landscape, drawn entirely in code.
- `scripts/audio.gd` — tiny UI tones synthesized at runtime.
- `scripts/ui_kit.gd` — palette, type, and style helpers.
- `icon.svg` — the project icon.

No external assets, downloads, fonts, or plugins are used. Everything visual is
drawn with Godot controls and `_draw`, and every sound is generated from a sine
wave at startup.

content.text:
Built **Common Ground**, a complete Godot 4.7.2 game about conflict mediation and perspective-taking.

### What it is
You chair three difficult conversations: a mill town divided over a polluted river, neighbors competing for a shared lot, and residents versus newcomers at a crowded school. Each side has a public **position** and hidden **interests** — the needs and fears underneath.

### Core loop
- **Listen** to reveal hidden needs and build goodwill, knowing the other side feels ignored.
- **Reassure** to keep someone at the table at the cost of a turn.
- **Connect** one need from each side to find genuine win-win solutions.
- False “bridges” cost goodwill; if either side reaches zero, they walk out.
- Bring all six needs onto common ground before round 14 ends.

The game teaches three broadly useful habits: hearing the interest behind a position, sharing attention, and looking for solutions that meet both fears instead of splitting the loss. It ends with a five-point field guide and a concrete real-world next step.

### Project details
- GL Compatibility renderer, no thread support, web-export ready.
- Main scene set in `project.godot`.
- All visuals drawn in code; all sounds synthesized at runtime; no external assets or plugins.
- Three chapters, intro/guide/result/field-guide screens, animations, generated audio, keyboard and mouse support.
- `README.md` includes run instructions.
- Verified with `godot --headless --path . --editor --quit` with no errors, plus automated win/failure tests for all scenarios.

Run with:

```bash
godot --path .
```
